name: ghe_danh_ca_vung_tau
sources: A motor fishing boat of Vũng Tàu with a beak (ghe mỏ nhọn): the class C5-T2-A of the Blue Book of Coastal Vessels, South Vietnam (Remote Area Conflict Information Center, Battelle, 1967; archive.org/details/DTIC_AD0664455), p. 329 and 330: 9 to 12 m long, 2.5 to 3 m wide, a draft of 1 m with its load, one diesel. Here: 11 m long and 2.6 m wide.

From the text of the book: two pointed ends, a sheer as a crescent from the stern to the beak of the bow, a low cabin on the gunwales over the engine, a hold with a deck before it, an open hold in the middle, a small deck in the bow, a canopy over the deck at the back, a rudder that is a long slab of wood on the curved sternpost.

The side view (the sheer, the stem, the sternpost, the places of the cabin, the canopy and the mast) is measured on the photo of p. 329, as parts of the length. The book has no lines and no section: the hull here is round, as deep as half its width (a guess).
The eyes: the Blue Book, p. 24 and 25 (figure 3, Vũng Tàu): an oval with a point at one end, black and white on red.
The colors are a choice (a blue hull with a red bottom and a red bow, as many boats of the south coast have): no source.
It is from edits only: no code of World knows this kind of model.
